text: Finally, when a brass shield fell upon a silver floor in the story, a hollow, metallic clang echoed through the house. <break time="0.8s" /> Usher was rocking gently from side to side, and as I bent closer, I heard him murmur quick, low words, as if unaware of my presence. <break time="0.8s" /> We have put her living in the tomb, he cried, I heard her first faint movements many days ago, but I dared not speak. <break time="0.8s" /> Springing to his feet, he shrieked, Madman, I tell you that she now stands outside the door. <break time="0.8s" /> As if by the power of his words, the huge, ancient doors slowly swung open, and there stood the tall, white figure of the Lady Madeline. <break time="0.8s" /> For a moment she stood trembling at the door, and there were signs of a bitter struggle in every part of her thin body. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, with a low, moaning cry, she fell heavily upon her brother, and both of them sank to the floor, never to rise again. <break time="0.8s" /> From that house I fled in terror, and when I looked back, a blood red moon was shining through the zigzag crack. <break time="0.8s" /> While I watched, the crack rapidly widened, the mighty walls rushed apart with a sound like a thousand waters, and the dark tarn at my feet closed silently over the fragments of the House of Usher.
